描述_EN: . [2] hundreds of millions of these relatively anonymous monoblocs have now been produced by different companies around the world. ‘monobloc’ is a term used to describe a type of lightweight stackable chair made from a single piece of plastic (often polypropylene). it was included in the inaugural exhibition, ‘values of design’, in the v&a gallery at design society in a section exploring cost, copies and the creation of value. today, the use of the term monobloc is more commonly associated with a type of cheap plastic chair which has no recognisable designer, yet has become global in its sale and distribution. colombo’s design included detachable feet, so that the height of the chair could be adjusted. both were fashioned from a single piece of compression-moulded fibreglass. its roots can be found in the late 1960s after polypropylene was first developed in 1963, opening up the possibility for plastics to be used in furniture design. joe colombo’s ‘universale’ chair however, designed from 1965-1967 (circ.887-1968) was an early attempt to fashion a monobloc using injection moulded plastic, the process used to manufacture most monoblocs today. although this type of monobloc has clear links to the above-mentioned early experiments in plastic chair designs, its exact origins are uncertain, with varying claims that the first monobloc originated in france, canada, or australia, either in the late 1970s or early 1980s. it was chosen for its similarity in shape to maarten baas’ ‘plastic chair in wood’, which has also been acquired for the v&a collection. they are both derided as ugly and cheap, but also celebrated as kitsch, and many designers have taken the anonymous monobloc as a source of design inspiration for new projects. using its own moulds, taizhou changheng trade co.,ltd is a manufacturer of a variety of different plastic products which include garden tools, furniture and food containers. a good example is maarten baas’s ‘plastic chair in wood’ [w.10-2015], which replicates the exact shape of a monobloc found in shanghai, yet is formed from carved elm wood. during this period many european designers began to experiment with how a chair might be formed out of a single piece of plastic. the chair was manufactured by taizhou changheng trade co.,ltd., based in taizhou, china. this chair was acquired as part of the shekou project, an international partnership between the v&a and china merchant shekou holdings (cmsk) to open a new cultural platform called design society in shekou. this particular monobloc armchair model bears the product code hs-011 and has a distinctive shape featuring three curved holes in the backrest and a carrying handle as well as three small lozenge shaped holes in the seat. most notably, helmut bätzner designed the bofinger stackable chair (circ.436 to 440-1970), between 1964 and 1965 and vico magistretti designed his ‘selene’ chair (circ.504-1973) a few years later in 1968.
描述_ZN: . [2]这些相对匿名的单体现在已经由世界各地的不同公司生产了数亿个。 单体 "是一个术语，用于描述一种由单块塑料（通常是聚丙烯）制成的轻型可堆叠椅子。 该作品被列入设计协会V&A画廊的首届展览 "设计的价值 "中，在探索成本、复制和创造价值的部分。 今天，monobloc这个词的使用更多的是与一种廉价的塑料椅子联系在一起，这种椅子没有可识别的设计师，但在其销售和分销方面已经成为全球性的。 科隆博的设计包括可拆卸的脚，这样椅子的高度就可以调整。 两者都是由一块压缩成型的玻璃纤维制成的。 其根源可以在20世纪60年代末找到，在1963年首次开发出聚丙烯后，为塑料用于家具设计提供了可能性。 然而，乔-科伦坡于1965-1967年设计的 "universale "椅子（circ.887-1968）是使用注塑塑料制造单体的早期尝试，也就是今天用于制造大多数单体的工艺。 虽然这种类型的monobloc与上述早期的塑料椅子设计实验有明显的联系，但它的确切起源是不确定的，有不同的说法，第一个monobloc起源于法国、加拿大或澳大利亚，要么在20世纪70年代末或80年代初。 它被选中是因为它的形状与Maarten Baas的 "木质塑料椅 "相似，后者也被V&A系列收购。 它们既被嘲笑为丑陋和廉价，但也被赞美为媚俗，许多设计师把无名单体作为新项目的设计灵感的来源。 泰州长恒贸易有限公司使用自己的模具，生产各种不同的塑料产品，包括花园工具、家具和食品容器。 一个很好的例子是Maarten Baas的 "塑料木椅"[W.10-2015]，它复制了一个在上海发现的单体的确切形状，但却是由雕刻的榆木制成的。 在此期间，许多欧洲设计师开始尝试如何用一块塑料形成一把椅子。 这把椅子是由位于中国泰州的泰州长恒贸易有限公司制造的。 这把椅子是作为Shekou项目的一部分被收购的，这是V&A和中国商人Shekholdings（cmsk）之间的国际合作，目的是在Shekou开设一个新的文化平台，称为设计社会。 这个特殊的单体扶手椅型号的产品代码为hs-011，具有独特的形状，在靠背上有三个弧形的孔和一个提手，在座椅上有三个菱形的小孔。 最值得注意的是，Helmut Bätzner在1964年和1965年之间设计了Bofinger可堆叠的椅子（Circ.436 to 440-1970），Vico Magistretti在几年后的1968年设计了他的'Selene'椅子（Circ.504-1973）。
